extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and recipients (institutional officials, PIs, grant administrators), especially those managing international collaborations, federal institution awards, and for-profit/SBIR-STTR awards
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of policy criteria and administrative requirements from NIH's Terms and Conditions (Part II Subpart B) covering collaborative international awards, grants to Federal and for-profit organizations, and SBIR/STTR program rules. Useful for applicants, institutional officials, and grant administrators to ensure compliance with award conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of support in RPPR for linked international awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary domestic recipient will provide an attestation of support within the international recipient’s RPPR confirming collaborative goals are being addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will be responsible for monitoring the RPPRs to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct document number and separate FFRs for linked international awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each linked international award uses a distinct document number/PMS subaccount and is required to submit separate Federal Financial Reports (FFR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebudgeting of awarded funds is not permitted between the prime and linked international awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: No rebudgeting between prime and linked international awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebudgeting of awarded funds is not permitted between the prime and linked international awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise specified in the NOFO and/or Notice of Award, collaborative international research awards, including any linked awards, will be excluded from automatic carryover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from automatic carryover for collaborative international awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative international research awards, including any linked awards, will be excluded from automatic carryover unless otherwise specified in the NOFO and/or Notice of Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception only if NOFO/NoA explicitly allows carryover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout requirement for both prime and linked international awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the prime domestic and linked international awards will be expected to complete the closeout requirement detailed in 8.6 Closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 8.6 for specific closeout steps and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to records for linked international award recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Linked international award recipients are required to provide access to copies of all lab notebooks, all data, and documentation that supports the research outcomes as described in the progress report, to NIH upon request, in accordance with 2 CFR 200.337.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access may be electronic; applies to materials supporting RPPR-reported outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required written agreement for collaborative international research
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations working together on a collaborative international research project must establish written agreements prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum, this agreement must include identification of roles/responsibilities of senior/key personnel at each site; procedures for directing and monitoring the research; procedures for managing disputes; a provision addressing ownership and disposition of data (including availability of cell lines/samples); expectations for authorship and co-authorship; and a provision requiring linked international award recipients to provide access to lab notebooks/data to the domestic (PF5/UF5) award recipient at least annually (which may be entirely electronic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include pass-through entity subrecipient oversight terms in collaborative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the domestic institution will not be serving as a pass-through entity, terms implementing the financial and administrative oversight requirements of subrecipients by pass-through entities (as detailed in 2 CFR 200.332) are not appropriate to include in the collaborative international research award agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium-like elements may be leveraged, but avoid pass-through/subrecipient oversight language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal institutions are eligible but must meet NOFO and statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal institutions are eligible to apply for NIH grants, including research project grants; specific eligibility will be stated in each NOFO and federal institutions also must meet the eligibility requirements of the grant program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHS organizational segments, other than IHS hospitals, may receive NIH grant support under exceptional circumstances only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance of responsibility for Federal institution awards
rubrics_metrics.description: A document that assures both the assumption of responsibility and authority to receive a grant must accompany each new and competing continuation application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assurance must be signed by the head of the responsible Federal department or independent agency or a designee who reports directly to the department or agency head; does not apply to VAMCs, Bureau of Prisons’ hospitals, IHS hospitals, or other PHS organizational segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: VA–university MOU requirements for joint appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators with joint appointments at a VAMC and an affiliated university must have a valid MOU that specifies the title of the investigator’s appointment, distribution of compensation, the responsibilities of the proposed investigator, and the percentage of effort available for research at each institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MOU must be signed by appropriate officials of the recipient and the VAMC, updated with each significant change and at least annually; the joint VA/university appointment constitutes 100 percent of their total professional responsibilities; NIH recognizes only such arrangements between a university and an affiliated VA hospital.

rubrics_metrics.name: AOR certification regarding VA–university joint appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature of the AOR of the submitting university on an application that includes such an arrangement certifies that the individual serves under a joint appointment documented in a formal MOU and there is no possibility of dual compensation or of an actual or apparent conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification supplements the AOR’s signature on the face page of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy: FCOI disclosure does not apply to Federal employees/agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements concerning disclosure of financial conflicts of interest do not apply to Federal employees and/or Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other Public Policy Requirements described in IIA apply to Federal recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment method for Federal institution grants (IPAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Office of Financial Management will pay grants and cooperative agreements to Federal departments and agencies through the Interagency Payment and Collection method (IPAC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt of an NIH award, Federal recipient institutions may send IPACs to NIH Agency Location Code (ALC) 75080031 for payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable/unallowable costs for Federal institutions governed by institutional policy or 2 CFR
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable and unallowable costs under grants to Federal institutions will be determined by the established policies of the institution, consistently applied, and the requirements of this subsection; in the absence of a governing organizational policy, the cost principles in 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart E, will apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional allowances under Kirschstein-NRSA fellowships may be requested by Federal institutions sponsoring fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs not provided to Federal institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs will not be provided to Federal institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional policy or applicable cost principles for other cost determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited cost types chargeable for Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Only four types of costs—consultant fees, subject costs, salary or fringe benefits, and travel costs—can be charged to NIH grants on behalf of Federal employees, whether by a recipient or a consortium participant, and under the conditions specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/recipients should advise any Federal employee to consult their agency ethics officials about outside activity approval and the employee’s ability to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for consultant fees for Uniformed Services medical personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultant fees are allowable only for medical personnel of the Uniformed Services of the United States (excluding PHS Commissioned Officers) when all of the following conditions are present: the employees are providing the kind and extent of medical services approved in the grant award; adequate numbers of qualified civilian personnel are not available; and the applicant provides prior written authorization from the proposed consultant’s commanding officer that they are authorized to work on the grant-supported activity during non-duty hours or while on authorized leave, and can be paid for their efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three listed conditions must be satisfied for consultant fees to be allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outpatient or subject costs for Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Outpatient or subject costs are allowable when the federal employee is an outpatient or subject under study in connection with grant-supported activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as allowable subject-related costs consistent with other human subject cost policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and fringe benefit payments for Federal employees are generally unallowable except in specified circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: In most circumstances no salary or fringe benefit payments may be made from NIH grant funds to support Federal employees; salary and fringe benefits payments may only be made when prior approval is obtained and the employee fits specified categories (temporary employee specifically hired, PHS Commissioned Officer or civil service employee with statutory authorization, PHS Commissioned Officer on LWOP meeting listed conditions, civil service employee on IPA meeting listed conditions, or certain part-time VA employees at VANPCs under defined rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed conditions include proportionality of pay to time devoted, written prior approval by NIH awarding IC for LWOP, certification/documentation of IPA assignments, prior determinations of no dual compensation or conflicts of interest, limits on IPA duration, and compliance with VA policies for VANPC differential payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel costs for Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel costs are allowable if the employee is working under a grant to a Federal institution; performing allowable reimbursable services as specified under Salary or Fringe Benefits; or attending an NIH grant-supported conference during non-duty hours, while in LWOP status, or while on detail to a State/local government, IHE, or other non-profit organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such payments must follow established organizational policy, be consistently applied, and ensure no actual or apparent conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment accountability for Federal institution awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will consider all nonexpendable personal property acquired under a grant awarded to a Federal institution as exempt (see 2 CFR Part 200.312) for purposes of determining accountability requirements of 2 CFR Part 200.313.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH reserves the right to require transfer of equipment, including title, to NIH or an eligible third party under conditions in 2 CFR Part 200.313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement requirements for Federal institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement under grants to Federal institutions is governed by the FAR and the recipient agency’s FAR supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FAR and agency supplement rules rather than non-Federal procurement standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property reporting and government assignment for Federal-employee inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions resulting from grants supporting activities of Federal employees under grants to Federal institutions must be reported simultaneously to NIH and to the employing agency under EO 10096 (as amended) and are subject to government assignment of rights in invention of government employee requirements of 37 CFR Part 401.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent applications/patents must identify the NIH award consistent with 37 CFR Part 401.14(f)(4); when VA is involved but not the grant recipient, the recipient must note VA’s involvement and provide a courtesy copy of the NIH notification to the appropriate VA office; NIH will notify recipient and VA about NIH’s interest in title/practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for Federal institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal institutions must electronically submit annual expenditure FFRs regardless of whether the award is subject to SNAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FFR submission rules and timelines in Part III and relevant sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: For-profit organizations eligible unless excluded by statute
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit organizations are eligible to apply under all NIH programs and support mechanisms unless specifically excluded by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific eligibility will be stated in each NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost principles for for-profit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no cost principles specifically applicable to grants to for-profit organizations; the cost principles for commercial organizations set forth in the FAR (48 CFR Part 31.2) generally are used to determine allowable costs under NIH grants to for-profit organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proprietary hospitals, use cost principles in 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix IX, Hospital Cost Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs allowed for for-profit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs, including de minimis costs when appropriate, are allowable under awards to for-profit organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Reimbursement of Indirect Costs for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: No profit/fee under NIH grants to for-profits except SBIR/STTR special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for grants awarded under the SBIR/STTR programs, under an NIH grant, no profit or fee will be provided to a for-profit organization, whether as a recipient or as a consortium participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profit/fee may be paid to a contractor under an NIH grant providing routine goods or services to the recipient, consistent with normal commercial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative requirements for for-profit recipients similar to non-profits
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit organizations generally are subject to the same administrative requirements as non-profit organizations, including those relating to personal property title and management, with exceptions or elaborations indicated where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See IIA sections for property management, procurement systems, and other standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment accountability and restrictions for for-profit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit recipients are nonexempt and subject to 2 CFR Part 200.313; they are permitted to retain title to equipment purchased under a research grant though NIH reserves the right to order transfer (including title) to NIH or an eligible third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For-profit recipients must not use NIH-funded equipment to provide services to non-Federal organizations for a fee in a way that competes unfairly with private companies; any user charges are program income and must be reported on the FFR. Conditions for sale of equipment are specified elsewhere in IIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property requirements for for-profit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual property requirements set forth in 37 CFR 401 apply to for-profit organizations; invention reporting requirements for for-profits differ somewhat from non-profits (assignment to third party does not require NIH approval but ongoing reporting is required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent authorized by law, the Federal government will not make public information disclosing a Federal government-supported invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income treatment for for-profit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit recipients, including those under SBIR/STTR, are subject to the additive alternative for the use of program income described in IIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH Standard Terms of Award for program income accounting and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating authorities and carryover for for-profit awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards to for-profit organizations are subject to NIH Standard Terms of Award; however, some mechanisms do not allow automatic carryover of unobligated balances of funds and the NIH awarding IC will specify disposition in the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an exception is not stated, IIA terms and conditions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit requirement for for-profit organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: A for-profit organization is required to have a non-Federal audit if, during its fiscal year, it expended a total of $750,000 or more under one or more Federal awards (as a direct recipient or consortium participant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audits must be completed and submitted to HHS Audit Resolution Division within 30 days after receipt of the auditor’s report(s), or 9 months after the end of the audit period, whichever is earlier. Organizations expending less than $750,000 are not required to have an annual audit but must make grant-related records available for review or audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor distribution and time-and-effort reporting for for-profit recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary and wage amounts charged to grant-supported projects must be based on an adequate labor distribution system; NIH requires for-profit organizations to conform with industry standards and, unless an alternate system is approved, to maintain a time-and-effort reporting system reflecting daily after-the-fact reporting of hours expended on individual projects or indirect activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system must record hours worked and hours absent and this information must be certified by an AOR no less frequently than every pay period.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Phase I objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I: The objective of this phase is to establish the technical merit and feasibility of proposed research or R&D efforts and to determine the quality of performance of the applicant before providing further Federal support in Phase II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I is for proof-of-concept and feasibility evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Phase II objective and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II: The objective is to continue the research or R&D efforts initiated in Phase I; funding will be based on Phase I results, scientific/technical merit, and commercial potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless Fast-Track, Phase II STTR applications may be submitted only after the Phase I award is made; only one Phase II award may be made for a specific project supported by a Phase I award; a Phase II recipient may receive one additional sequential Phase II (Phase IIB) in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct to Phase II eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For small businesses that have already demonstrated scientific and technical merit and feasibility but have not received a Phase I SBIR or STTR for that project, NIH can issue a SBIR Direct to Phase II award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct to Phase II accepts Phase II applications regardless of funding source for prior proof-of-principle work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II submission timing expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: For small businesses that have received a Phase I SBIR or STTR, NIH expects non Fast-Track Phase II applications to be submitted within the first six receipt dates following expiration of the Phase I budget period (normally 2 years beyond completion of the Phase I award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to timing expectations unless otherwise noted in NOFO or IC guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase IIB and CRP program purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase IIB Competing Renewal awards are for projects requiring extraordinary time and effort (e.g., regulatory approval, complex instrumentation, clinical research tools); the Commercialization Readiness Pilot (CRP) facilitates transition of previously funded Phase I/IIB projects to commercialization by providing additional support for later-stage R&D and product development not typically supported through Phase II or Phase IIB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility limited to prior Phase II award recipients as specified; check specific NOFOs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR primary employment requirement for PD/PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Under SBIR, the PD/PI must have their primary employment with the small business concern (more than one half of the PD/PI’s time at the SBC) at the time of award and for the duration of the project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations for Phase I allowable under exceptional circumstances with written approval by awarding IC; deviations for Phase II are extremely rare and require written approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR PD/PI employment and effort requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under STTR the PD/PI may have primary employment with either the SBC or the collaborating research institution; on an STTR project, the PD/PI must devote at least 10 percent of their time to the STTR project and must have a formal appointment with or commitment to the SBC (official relationship; need not include salary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PD/PI is not an employee of the SBC they must be officially affiliated in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR partnering research institution workshare requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The STTR program requires that at least 40 percent of the STTR research project is to be conducted by the SBC and at least 30 percent of the work is to be conducted by the single partnering research institution through a formal, cooperative arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The STTR grant is awarded to the SBC, which disburses appropriate funding to the research institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR allows subcontracting; STTR requires formal partner
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBIR program allows subcontracting and does not require partnering, so the SBC may conduct the entire SBIR project without outside collaboration; the STTR program requires formal partnership with a single non‑profit research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan project organization according to program rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR program mobility between program/phase solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may 'switch' programs to any active and open NIH SBIR or STTR solicitation, including Parent solicitations and targeted funding opportunities, but must comply with the policies for the program and NOFO to which they submit the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See SBIR Life Cycle Certification and STTR Life Cycle Certification sections for requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Fast-Track process for SBIR/STTR
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Fast-Track application process allows Phase I and Phase II grant applications to be submitted and reviewed together and receive a single rating, expediting award decisions for meritorious projects with high commercialization potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to consult with NIH program staff to ensure Fast-Track is appropriate; see the SF424 (R&R) SBIR/STTR Application Guide for submission details.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR eligibility: U.S. small business concern criteria (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only United States small business concerns (SBCs) are eligible to submit SBIR and STTR applications. An SBC must be organized for profit, have a place of business located in the United States, operate primarily within the United States or make a significant contribution to the U.S. economy, and meet specified ownership and size requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules include acceptable legal forms, ownership/control tests (more than 50% owned/controlled by U.S. individuals or certain entity ownership structures), affiliate rules, and an employee cap of not more than 500 employees; NIH will request an SBA size determination if eligibility is unclear.
